convoLines.text: "What do you make of all this? Really. Can't sit still, you know?"
"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."
"Still on what you make of all this."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Gotta keep moving."
"Naomi owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
You show them Wild Ginger — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I keep turning over the last thing Naomi said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here? That's my read."
"Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset."
"Still on your useful old-life skills."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Not that it matters."
"Naomi is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Wild Ginger — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I do push-ups at dawn. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Naomi's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Alright. Catch you later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About what happened to my taken kin — You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Liam? Just... be straight with me."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.

"It's my father, Liam. Went in the Taking. He never did anything interesting except keep us all alive. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Good talking."
"Naomi always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
You show them Wild Ginger — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 3 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"I'm picking up Naomi's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 3 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Elias shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You called this the end of the world. We're still here, though. That's either something, or it's us."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Luz has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff. Anyway, I should move."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
"Take your time."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I tried the Wild Ginger like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Nobody's worked where the pawpaw grows thick in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Someone has to make decisions here. I'm just saying — it might as well be someone who knows how.
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Rosa digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+967 kcal to the pantry.)
"I've been the one in the corner with the plan. Might as well be the one in the middle with it."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what they want."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Ji was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."

"As I said — Still on what's been happening."

"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that question."

"You said patience was your old-life superpower — really waiting, without fidgeting. Still your answer?"
"Anyway." A small smile.

"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Prickly Pear today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Luz has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."

"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"I can't reach this properly. Could you take a look?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.

"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that favor."
"This was good." They mean it.
«ما هذا المكان؟ أين نحن؟»
«هذا صحيح.» — Omar translates: "This is right." They nod back, slowly.
«أنت إنسان طيب.» — Omar translates: "You are a kind person." A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«ما قصرت، الله يخليك.» — Omar translates: "You've done plenty — God keep you." You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «وين ننام هنا؟» — Omar translates: "Where do we sleep here?"
«عندك أكل؟» — Omar translates: "Do you have food?"
Ryuichi laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — مضبوط، كلامك صحيح.." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
